body: AI autonomy for a coastal-denial network of unmanned surface vessels.
why: US autonomy software combined with allied hardware is a repeatable export model.

title: CBO: Golden Dome could cost $1.2T over 20 years; DoW estimate $185B to 2035
body: Independent estimates range from $175B (White House) to $3.6T (AEI) depending on the design.
why: A huge, contested budget line. Its political survival will shape space and missile-defense startups.

title: FY27 request: $54.6B for DAWG and $53.6B for Drone Dominance
body: DAWG rises from $225M. The drone effort includes $39.2B for autonomous systems procurement and domestic production plus $14.4B for counter-unmanned systems.
why: The biggest budget shift toward autonomy ever. Follow it through Congress.

title: PitchBook: defense-tech VC hits $69.5B over the trailing 12 months
body: Q1 set a record at $19.8B across 262 deals; Q2 brought $16.4B across 249. Autonomy took 42.1% of Q2. Eleven public listings reopened exits.
why: Money concentrates in mega-rounds and seed; mid-stage is hard.

title: Space Force picks 12 firms, including SpaceX, Anduril, Lockheed and True Anomaly, for space-based interceptor prototypes
body: Awards total up to $3.2B, with a demonstration due by 2028.
why: Missile defense, once the primes' preserve, now includes new entrants.

title: Ukraine to field 25,000 ground robots for frontline logistics
body: About 280 companies make 550+ ground-vehicle models, running 10,000+ logistics missions a month.
why: The clearest demand signal yet for ground autonomy, years ahead of the US.

title: DoD components face an 'aggressive' timeline to move onto Maven Smart System
body: Deputy Secretary Feinberg pushed Maven toward a department-wide program of record.
why: How a vendor becomes the standard; once every command runs on Maven, replacing it is very hard.

title: Germany and Ukraine sign a €4B package that includes joint drone production
body: Part of Europe's push to scale autonomous-systems manufacturing.
why: Ukrainian know-how plus European money is becoming a production base that will compete with US firms.

title: Saronic raises $1.75B Series D at $9.25B
body: For autonomous surface vessels and shipyard capacity.
why: Naval autonomy is the next large hardware market.

title: RAND: crosscutting insights for the drone-dominance push
body: Large numbers of attritable, adaptable unmanned systems now cost orders of magnitude less than traditional platforms.
why: Research support for the cheap-mass thesis.

title: Shield AI raises $1.5B Series G at $12.7B
body: Led by Advent and co-led by JPMorgan; Blackstone added $500M of preferred equity.
why: AI pilot software is valued as its own layer, separate from airframes.

title: Anduril and Palantir reported to be leading Golden Dome's software layer
body: Teamed with SpaceX for parts of the constellation; they lead the software that links sensors to interceptors.
why: The command core of the decade's largest program went to newcomers.

title: PLA demonstrates the 'Atlas' swarm: one vehicle launches 96 drones; claims of 200 per operator
body: The drones fly an autonomous anti-jamming path-planning algorithm tested under electromagnetic interference.
why: The pacing threat for US swarm and counter-swarm programs. It drives requirements.

title: Drone Dominance Gauntlet I: 25 vendors compete, 11 selected
body: Held at Fort Benning. About 100 operators flew each system after two hours of training.
why: Easy to learn and cheap to buy beat exotic performance.

title: First known microwave kill of a jam-proof fiber-optic drone
body: Epirus Leonidas disabled a fiber-optic-guided drone in a live-fire demo.
why: Fiber-optic drones made jamming obsolete in parts of Ukraine; microwave weapons and interceptors are the answer.

title: Hanwha Defense USA and HavocAI agree to co-develop 200-ft autonomous surface vessels
body: Korean shipbuilding paired with US collaborative-autonomy software. HavocAI later advanced to Navy MUSV at-sea testing.
why: Foreign shipyards plus US autonomy could relieve the Navy's capacity crunch.
